newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Arbed says taking "leap forward" with Spanish deal.
newsitem.headline: Arbed says taking "leap forward" with Spanish deal.

text.p: Luxembourg steel firm Arbed, chosen by Spanish state holding firm AIE to take a 35 percent stake in Spanish steel company CSI, said on Thursday the deal would boost Arbed's position in Europe and the world.

"A new cross-border partnership will be created which will integrate the major part of the steel industry of the Iberian peninsular in the Arbed strategy," chairman Joseph Kinsch said in his first public comments on the deal.
"With this our company will take a new leap forward in the European and world steel hierarchy and will reinforce its positions on all the markets of the globe," he added.

Under the terms of the deal which was announced earlier this week, CSI - Corporacion Siderurgica Integral - will increase capital by 129.0 billion pesetas, with Arbed subscribing the whole issue for a 35 percent stake in the Spanish firm.
CSI will then invest about 100 billion pesetas of that amount in stakes in Arbed companies.
Kinsch was speaking before steel workers and government ministers at a ceremony to mark the closure of Luxembourg's last blast furnace, at Arbed's Esch-Belval site.
When the furnace has ceased all activity by the end of August, Arbed will have completed the conversion of its long products sector in Luxembourg to electric steel making.
Kinsch said that through the CSI partnership, Arbed would reach a size where it could produce 17 million tonnes of steel a year.
Based on 1996 figures, Arbed and CSI's combined crude steel output of 11.8 and 4.5 million tonnes respectively would have ranked them second in Europe after British Steel, analysts say.
